page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.2xlarge is a general-purpose instance powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on the ARM64 architecture, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 model running at 2.8 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage.

Benchmark data indicates solid general-purpose performance, highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score in the top 10% and a strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 14.48 GB/s. Most other compute metrics, including Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores, fall within the average range. Cryptographic performance is a relative bottleneck, with the PassMark CPU encryption test scoring in the bottom 25%. Large-block memory write bandwidth reaches 86.22 GB/s, while static web serving throughput averages 19.89 GB/s.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps, making it highly optimized for network and EBS-reliant workloads. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation deliver competitive resource density and high memory performance without the overhead of hyperthreading. This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including database operations, static web serving, redis caching, and light multi-threaded applications.
